Claire — thanks, excited to move this to a tight MAP. Attached is a draft (Redwood-MAP-draft-v1.pdf) and a live checklist in Drive. Key highlights below; I've mapped owners and expected evidence.

Draft MAP summary (high level)
- Objective: Pilot to validate inference quality + production economics on a 2-week staging sprint, then a 3-week pilot at customer scale.
- Core acceptance dimensions: Functionality (concordance on 200 canonical prompts), Performance (p95 < 350ms for 512-token avg call under target QPS), Reliability (99.5% availability during pilot windows), Security (no PHI retention beyond session TTL), Cost (tokens/unit under threshold).
- Exit gates (must all be green to proceed to roll):
  1) Concordance >= 92% across sample prompt set (owner: Novus / Claire)
  2) p95 latency under 350ms at agreed baseline load (owner: Redwood / Marcus)
  3) Error rate < 1% sustained over 48h (owner: Redwood / Karthik)
  4) SOC2 evidence & logging proof-of-delivery to procurement (owner: Novus / procurement contact)
  5) No unresolved high-severity security items (owner: Redwood Security, coord via Laura)

Acceptance tests (examples)
- Functional: 200-case concordance harness (pass threshold 92%); run nightly with diff report.
- Performance: 1-hour sustained run at pilot QPS with KV cache warm, measure p50/p95/p99 and tail behaviors.
- Reliability: 72-hour smoke run with inject faults (planned regen) to verify fallback model variant behavior.
- Security: Data retention audit log showing session-level TTL enforcement; access log snapshot.

Timeline & immediate next steps
- Today: share draft (attached) and Drive link.
- 4/27: incorporate procurement feedback + security checklist (Laura)
- 4/28–5/07: run initial concordance + perf runs (owner: Novus + Redwood test harness)
- 5/10: MAP review checkpoint and sign-off or redline

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP outline); MAP-final-checklist-v2.xlsx (live checklist template)

Tessa — quick internal sync notes after reviewing the draft:

1) Latency SLO: We should specify request-size buckets (<=256 tokens, 257–1024 tokens) and provide separate p95 targets. For Novus's average prompt mix I'd recommend p95 <= 300ms for <=256 tokens and p95 <= 420ms for 257–1024 tokens.
2) Concordance harness: add a stratified sample by intent type (diagnostic, triage, admin) so we don't bias to the easiest prompts.
3) Reliability test: add an owner for rollback playbook verification (Marcus).

I'll slot Marcus for kernel-config tuning and a whitespace run on 4/29 to validate batch sizing. Laura — can your security checklist include a note about telemetry retention period and anonymization steps? Claire — if procurement needs a specific artifact name, tell us and we'll attach.
